entries.title: Remaining leads from the survey of comparable agent orchestrators (Oct 2026)
entries.body:
Leads borrowed from comparable open-source agent orchestrators, surveyed in October 2026 (first imported from issue #671).
Nothing here is a commitment; these are leads to triage.
The orch checked each against the code on 2026-11-17: ideas lym has built or that proved moot are dropped,
partly built ones name only what is still open, and the eight most worth doing are notes of their own in this project.
Each bullet names its source project and the lym module it would touch.

## Plan validation and concurrency (quarry, Plan-Write, board)

- **Typed scope operations on cards** (foremerge): each scope carries an additive or breaking operation,
  and deterministic rules flag colliding pairs even when files do not overlap.
  Worth comparing against board labels and the alignment gate.
- **Symbol leases between concurrent tasks** (Fusion, ORCH): expiring leases on symbol keys serialize overlapping tasks,
  with a deterministic tie-break; lym keeps overlapping tasks apart by board labels.
- **Commit-time reservation guard** (ntm): a pre-commit hook refuses a commit touching what another task holds; needs leases first.
- **Criterion amendment ledger** (oh-my-claudecode): a card's acceptance text changes only through a recorded amendment in weft.

## Review (burler, Bouncer)

- **Quorum of differently-angled judges** (ccswarm): lym fans out lenses but has no quorum vote for high-risk segments.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's parent orch can be asked to see and veto each Code-Review round and each drift judge ruling
  (`loom.code.review_ask_parent`, `drift.judge_ask_parent`); that is one extra judge, not a quorum.
- **Risk tier by changed paths** (yylo): globs over sensitive paths choose the review depth and the gate scope.

## Engine, recipes and governance (shed, tender, orch, board)

- **Cross-run quarantine** (Bernstein): a task that fails three times across runs is held, unless the failures were the host's.
- **Fork a run from a step with a tree snapshot** (Bernstein): `shed goto` moves the cursor but does not restore the warp tree.
- **Warm retry guarded by a workspace hash** (Bernstein): resume the native session only when the tree is unchanged.
  Partly met since `dfade5f9a`: a run agent whose session a crash, reboot or killed pane ended resumes it (engines with a `SessionResumer`, so not Codex);
  no tree hash guards that resume, and a retry after a timeout or a finished run still starts fresh.
- **Evidence reuse by input identity** (yylo): verify is skipped on the same tree; a changed review prompt could rerun only the review.
- **Guidance at the next step boundary** (Conductor): a queue of operator guidance for the next producer's prompt.
  Partly met since 2026-11-19: `loom.notify_parent_on` mails the run's parent when a named row is reached,
  so the parent can brief that row's agent as it starts; there is still no queue of guidance lym itself folds into the prompt.
- **Batched operator questions with recorded assumptions** (Spec Kit `/clarify`, Conductor): Discussion-Write asks at most a few ranked questions,
  each with a recommended answer, and records unanswered ones as assumptions.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's autonomous agents put their questions to the run's parent orch, not to the operator in their pane.
  Discussion asks in its pane only when `loom.discussion.interactive` is `true`, which is off by default and forced off by autonomy mode (`30ed1ee58`),
  so this lead concerns an interactive Discussion only.
- **Rate-limit wait**: the orch watcher wakes the orch after a usage reset; tender itself schedules no resume.
- **Standing goals and scheduled routines** (ORCH, CAO, Fusion): periodic triage, dependency bumps or `selfreport` sweeps.

## Agent sessions (reed, shuttle)

- **Waiting-for-input signal** (agent-of-empires): shuttle has an awaiting-input state; screen heuristics still decide readiness and startup.
- **Reference status patterns and a paste pitfall** (CAO): compare its regexes and its tmux bracketed-paste note with shuttle's readiness and creel inject.
- **Context forecasting** (ntm): the orch cycles its context; Webster's Master and the loom driver do not, and nothing forecasts.
- **Staggered spawns** (ntm): space Webster forks and batten fan-out by learned rate limits.

## Observability (report, weft)

- **Hash-chained run journal** (Bernstein): a hash chain over producer outputs makes an archived run self-verifying.
- **Unverified-completion rate** (Bernstein): a `lym report` view of completions with no test or gate behind them.
- **Commit-to-record links** (AgentNote): weft links to warp by a `Warp-SHA:` trailer; a note or trailer on each warp commit could link back.
- **Run diff** (ccswarm): `lym report` comparing two archived runs' timelines and token use.
- **OpenTelemetry spans per producer** (Conductor).

## Operator attention (orch, dobby, reed)

- **Attention feed with acknowledgement states** (ntm): dobby's wait reminders have no seen, snoozed or acknowledged states.

## Discussion review (Discussion-Write, stencils, pattern)

- **Requirements-quality checklist** (Spec Kit `/checklist`): items with IDs the Discussion-review judge answers one by one.
- **Fixed analysis categories** (Kiro): inconsistency, ambiguity, conflicts, unstated assumptions and missing edge cases as named lenses.
- **PATTERN rules handed to reviewers** (Spec Kit constitution): its rules as numbered MUSTs in plan and code review prompts.
- **Glob-scoped steering** (Kiro): stencils pull per-area guidance chosen by the paths of a plan's glyphs.

Note `pr-ask-live-pane-test` is folded in only to be closed: it asks for a test of the parent-review ask this task removes.

Bundled from the notes below; each part keeps its note's text.

# Take the parent out of PR-Review; the earlier reviewers must catch what it finds

Imported from [issue #223](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/223).

## Seen (operator, 2026-11-24)

Today the parent orch can be asked to review at PR-Review, and the operator has used that a lot.
The operator now judges it a bad idea, for two reasons.

PR-Review is the very last gate, and it belongs to the human.
When a run reaches it, everything the LLMs and LoomYard can do should already be done.

A parent is also the wrong reviewer.
Asking the parent, which is the orchestrator, to review a Discussion or code is work for the orchestrator, and it costs more than a cold-start agent.
The reviewers a run already has should catch what the parent catches.

## Decision (operator, 2026-11-26)

No agent reviews the pull request any more: when the PR is made, the agents are done.
What a parent finds when asked to review a PR must be found and fixed before the PR;
the checks that catch it are in the notes on reviewing the Describe text and on closing a task's scope at Code-Review.

## Idea

Take every agent out of PR-Review and add no seat in its place.

- Remove the parent's ask and re-ask from PR-Review in `internal/landingshed` and `internal/loomcli`.
- Remove PR-Review's own interactive session and its findings path: `pr_reviewer`, `lym loom pr-findings`, `pr_review_small_max`, `pr_review_ask_parent` and `pr_review_parent_timeout_min`.
- The row keeps only the mechanics the PR mode needs (see the note on the PR mode's three settings).
- Rely on the cold-start reviewers.
  The `review-code` fan already holds `code-scope`, which traces every decision of the record to a change in the diff and flags a decision no change builds, besides `code-correctness`, `code-affected-set` and `code-tests`.
  Read first which lenses the C# hubs run in `review-code` today, since the hub's own `lenses.yaml` and the C# layer can change the fan.
- Decide what a run does with a commit pushed to the PR branch by hand while it waits.


# A PR mode that registers the PR and approves it at once, with no agent under the block

Imported from [issue #224](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/224).

## Seen (operator, 2026-11-24)

The operator often wants a pull request registered on GitHub without looking at it.
With a beam, say P1, and several tasks under it, the operator wants each task to land as a PR that is approved at once and merged into the beam.
When all of P1 is done, one PR goes from P1 into its parent (P0 or root), and it lists every member PR.
That lets the operator backtrack and see how the work got where it is.

## Decision (operator, 2026-11-26)

The PR block has three modes, and no LLM takes part in any of them:

- Manual: the PR is made and waits for the operator's own review and approval, as PR-Review is meant today.
- None: no PR; the row passes, as `pull_request` off does today.
- Trail (`pull_request: trail`, operator 2026-11-26): the PR is made and merged at once, with no agent and no human, so the beam's PR history can be backtracked.

How the three modes are configured is not decided yet.

## Idea

- Trail: the PR is made, no agent is spawned, and Finalize merges it at once, as it does today after the operator's `lym loom pr-continue`; merging a PR without an approval has long worked in lym.
- A beam's own PR lists its member PRs.
  `Rewrite a beam's pull request description after each member landing` (`1cd11ee5e`) may already do part of this; read what it writes before adding more.
- Manual waits for a human approval whatever the autonomy, which covers the note on autonomy and PR-Review.
- Read first where `beam.yaml` `pull_request` is read (`internal/landingshed`, `internal/pullrequest`) and how a run reaches Finalize today when a PR is approved.


# Autonomy: let PR review stay with the operator for one beam

Imported from [issue #217](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/217).

`beam.yaml: autonomy` is one switch for both halts and PR-Review requests. A hub wants the orch to settle halts on the prime autonomously while pull requests into the prime's branch (main) still wait for the operator's approval. Today that needs autonomy off, which also sends every halt to the operator, or autonomy on with the orch holding PR-Review by hand. Proposal: a separate key, such as `autonomy_pr_review: false`, so PR-Review requests on that beam or the prime go to the operator while halts stay autonomous.

## Issue comment, 2026-11-24

Seen again, with a merge into the prime's branch:

- The prime runs with `autonomy: true`, and the hub wants pull requests into main to wait for a human approval.
- The task `import-project-names` reached PR-Review; the parent answered the parent-review ask `--satisfied` and told the PR-Review agent by creel that landing waits on the operator's approval.
- `lym loom pr-continue` ran anyway about a minute later, and Finalize squash-merged the pull request into main once its gate passed, with no human approval on GitHub.

A message to the PR-Review agent is no way to hold a landing under autonomy: the satisfied answer alone ends the review.

Expected: a setting, per beam and for the prime, that keeps autonomy for halts but makes PR-Review wait for a human approval of the pull request (for example a GitHub approving review) before `pr-continue` or Finalize may merge.

# No tmux-tier test sends parent-review ask from a live non-orch pane

## Seen

`failed-ask-hides-satisfied` (issue 213) left out its item 3: no test runs `lym loom parent-review ask` from a live non-orch reed strand pane.
That is the path that failed twice on 2026-11-23 in the mo hub (creel refused the LOOM signature), and the fix (708cdadc5) is pinned only below the tmux tier.

## Idea

A tmux-tier test: a built lym binary in a reed strand pane, a hub with a pull request record under autonomy, and a live orch strand that receives the post; assert the ask is delivered and the parent's answer lets `pr-continue` end the review.



# README display

The board README shows each beam's pull-request setting (task `readme-beam-modes`); show the three modes there.

entries.title: Review the Describe text in its row, keep LoomYard terms out, sync the PR body
entries.body:
This task builds items 1 and 2 of the Describe-text note's Idea; items 3 to 6 belong to the task that closes scope at Code-Review.
No agent reviews the pull request any more (task `pr-modes-no-agent`), so the Describe text is the last text an LLM checks.

Bundled from the notes below; each part keeps its note's text.

# The Describe text names no LoomYard terms, except the Created using block

Imported from [issue #227](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/227).

## Seen (operator, 2026-11-24)

An analysis of the parent's PR-Review findings in the C# hubs found that about 12 findings were internal process or tool names in the PR text: "item 3 of the task", "the test scoper cannot run C# tests there", "the task's branch point", "The board entry proposed", "The parent recorded...".
The stencil that writes the description (`landing-template-describe`) does not forbid them, so the parent had to tell the Describe session so in each hub.
In one run the parent noted its own earlier instruction had caused it.

The operator's rule: LoomYard, and anything from it, does not belong in the Describe text.
The one exception is the "Created using" block at the bottom.

## Idea

Keep LoomYard's vocabulary out of the description the Describe row writes, and let lym hold it.

- Add the rule to the Describe stencil: the description names no board, task, Sketch, decision record, parent, orch, scoper, gate, tier, perch or lym term, and no "item N of the task".
- Let the Describe row's mechanical gate (`NewDescriptionGate`, which runs `summaryparser.ValidateDescription`) refuse such a term outside the credit block, with the refusal naming the term and the line.
- Leave the credit block as it is: the `credit` keys in `landing.yaml` append it, and the term check skips it.
- Read first how the credit block is appended to the description, and which words the check can match without refusing a repository's own legitimate names.
- The issue on reviewing the Describe text covers claims and missing content; this issue covers the vocabulary.


# Review the Describe text inside the Describe row, and catch the rest of what the parent finds at PR-Review earlier

Imported from [issue #225](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/225).

## Seen (operator, 2026-11-24)

In the C# repos on one machine, a parent asked to review a PR always finds something.
That points to a design flaw: if the parent finds something, an earlier quality check missed it.

The operator's guess was that the delivered code often does not cover everything the Discussion's decision record asked for.
The operator judges the finding below, that most of it is the PR text, as not very important, and that it is solved by reviewing the Describe text too.

## What the parent finds (analysis, 2026-11-24)

An analysis read 25 PR-Review rounds with findings, across four hubs; one more hub had no PR-Review records.
About 65 findings are itemised in readable text; about 29 more were in scratchpad files that no longer exist.
The task worktrees and the Sketches of the landed tasks are gone, so the only full source is each hub's creel mail journal, and the gate attributions are mostly inferred.
The full report is a local file and is not committed.

- About half of the findings (32 of 65) are about the PR description, not the code:
  internal process or tool names in the text (12), wrong or overreaching claims (12), and content the task asked for that the text omits (8).
- The rest are tests missing or too costly (10), wrong behaviour (8), doc or comment drift (7) and scope the Sketch did not hold (8).
- The operator's guess holds only in part: 4 of 25 rounds cite a Sketch or task requirement that was missed, and all four concern the PR text or scope, not code behaviour.
- A finding is often sent twice because the agent edits the summary file but not the GitHub PR body (about 5 rounds).

## Idea

The Describe row writes the change description, which becomes the PR title, the PR body and the landing commit message.
It is a seat table (`DescribeTable` in `internal/landingshed/describe.go`) whose session already reads the decision record, and its only gate is mechanical (`ValidateDescription`); no agent reviews what the text says.

1. Review the Describe text inside the Describe row with a second agent, an assistant seat, and send its findings back to the writer; Describe is the last step that uses an LLM, so no review runs after it.
   The reviewer checks that the text names no internal process or tool (board, task, scoper, Sketch, decision record, "item N of"), that every claim holds against the diff and the task's report or measurements, and that every deliverable the Sketch says to state in the description is there.
   The mechanical gate stays in front of it.
   This covers the 32 findings about the text.
2. Sync the GitHub PR body from the description on every push, and verify the two match (about 5 re-sent rounds).
3. Run the mutation or redundancy tier on every C# task, and give the Plan a tier0 cost budget (10 test findings).
4. Have Discussion record what the parent will check: measured figures, doc statements and test intent.
5. Let a Code-Review finding the parent already ruled in scope reach a fixer; today a decision finding spawns none.
6. Re-check a constant quoted in a doc when the case it was measured on changes.

The issue on taking the parent out of PR-Review leaves these checks to the cold-start reviewers, so they must run before PR-Review, and a task's scope closes at its first Code-Review round (see the issue on closing a task's scope).


# The GitHub PR body is not updated when the description file changes

Imported from [issue #228](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/228).

## Seen

An analysis of the parent's PR-Review findings in the C# hubs found that the same findings were sent again in about five rounds.
The agent fixed the description file but the pull request's body on GitHub was not updated, so the parent read the old text again.
Seen in five separate rounds across several runs.

## Why it makes no sense

The description file is the one source of the PR title and body.
A PR whose body differs from the file the run holds is wrong from the first push, and a review round is spent on text that has already been fixed.

## Idea

Make the PR body follow the description file on every push, and refuse to end a round while the two differ.

- Read first where `pr update` runs for a task's pull request, and which path writes the description file without calling it (`lym beam describe` runs the `pr update` sequence for a beam; check the task path).
- After each push, compare the GitHub PR body with the file, and update it or halt with a way forward naming the difference.
- Add a test that edits the description file after the PR exists and expects the body to follow on the next push.


# Describe halts failed on an uninformative shuttle run outcome timeout

Imported from [issue #244](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/244).

The Describe step halted the run as `failed` with anomaly `producer-hard-failure` and the message `shedadapters: Describe (seats): shuttle run outcome timeout`.

Why it is abnormal:
- The note carries no detail on which timeout elapsed, how long the shuttle run had been going, or whether the agent was still working.
- A timeout on a seated shuttle run is classed as a hard failure, so the run stopped as `failed` rather than being resumed or escalated.
- The next attempt of the same step completed (`Describe / done`) about 34 minutes later, which suggests the timeout was not a defect in the producer's work.

What to do:
- Include the elapsed time, the timeout limit and the shuttle run's last known state in the halt reason.
- Decide whether a shuttle outcome timeout should be a retryable or `blocked` stop instead of `failed`.

Provenance: task `retire-d9`; note loom-halt.md.


# Describe seat waits out the full timeout after an operator interrupt, then halts as hard failure

Imported from [issue #241](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/241).

The Describe producer (seats engine) halted the run as `failed` with `shuttle run outcome timeout`, after its agent session sat held for about 28 minutes with no output.

Sequence from the trace:

```
22:15:05 shuttle: run started role=describe
22:16:51 shuttle: session state state=idle-stalled cause=interrupt
22:16:53 shuttle: session state state=busy cause=turn
22:16:57 shuttle: turn end held, output files missing
22:16:57 shuttle: held turn end of a turn the operator started; no hold notice
22:16:57 shuttle: session state state=idle-stalled cause=no-output loop=held
22:45:06 shuttle: run finished outcome=timeout cleanedUp=false
22:45:29 shed: step refused kind=producer transient="" error="shedadapters: Describe (seats): shuttle run outcome timeout"
```

The halt note reads `loom halted failed at Describe`, `anomaly: producer-hard-failure`, 12 history entries.

Why this is abnormal:
- The operator interrupted the agent once and typed into the pane, which made the turn "operator-started".
  lym then held the turn end without a hold notice and waited silently until the run timeout.
- The session was `idle-stalled` for the whole wait, and nothing re-prompted the agent for its missing output files or surfaced the state to the operator.
- The timeout was then recorded as a hard failure with `transient=""`, although the cause was an interrupted session and not a producer defect.
- `cleanedUp=false` on the finished run, and the strand was stopped with `live=true` afterwards.

Suggested fix: when a turn end is held for missing output files after an operator-started turn, send the agent a reminder or hand the pane back to the operator with a visible notice instead of waiting out the whole timeout.
Classify a timeout that follows an operator interrupt as resumable, not as `producer-hard-failure`.

Provenance: task `transient-tripout-overpull`, from `loom-halt.md`.




## From issue #255

Imported from [issue #255](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/255).

The Describe step wrote a pull request body that names lym, LoomYard and another task, and the run's docs carried the same kind of internal names.
Code-Review approved the diff, and PR-Review raised the leak afterwards as a send-back with three findings: one BLOCKING (the pull request body names lym internals), one MEDIUM (two document sections describe lym internals), one NIT.
The same class of leak had already been fixed by hand-written commits earlier in the run, such as a rewrite of a document to describe test tiers by what they run instead of through the gate.

This is abnormal because the output goes into a repository that does not know lym: a pull request body and repository documents should not name lym, LoomYard or other tasks.
Neither the Describe nor the Code-Review instructions caught it, so the leak cost a PR-Review send-back and a second Code-Bouncer, Code-Burler-Review and Code-Burler-Fix cycle.

What to do:
- Tell the Describe step, and any step that writes repository documents, not to name lym, LoomYard, gates, or other tasks in a pull request body or a repository file.
- Have Code-Review check documents and the pull request body for such names, so the finding comes before approval and not from PR-Review.

Provenance: task `dead-code-and-timing-docs`; notes `pr-review-send-back-1.md`, `loom-halt.md` (history only).

entries.title: Machine stops, dead judges and idle seats are not producer failures
entries.body:
Bundled from the notes below; each part keeps its note's text.

# Gate fixer interrupted by a machine stop is reported as dead (timeout)

Imported from [issue #248](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/248).

## What happened

A row gate spawned a cold fixer, and the machine rebooted under a minute later.
The run was re-stepped more than two days after that.
The loop's reconcile had stopped the fixer's shuttle run, but the gate fixer's record still read live.
The restarted driver waited on that record, classified it `dead` with reason `timeout`, and told the writer:

> The cold fixer ended without a reply (timeout); any change it left uncommitted is in the worktree.

The interrupted-stop detail, from the first entry after the reboot:

```
loop exit: not recorded, since no process marked the loop's exit, and the machine has booted since the loop started, so a stop of the machine likely ended it; (...) stopped shuttle runs: ly:<slug>:gate-fixer; left runs whose output files all exist: ly:<slug>:darn
```

The fixer's shuttle `run.json` (excerpt):

```
"createdAt": "2026-11-23T19:19:20Z",
"outcome": "stopped",
"roleKey": "gate-fixer",
"interrupted": true
```

The gate fixer's `records.json` after the resume (excerpt):

```
"spawnedAt": "2026-11-23T19:19:27Z",
"status": "dead",
"deadReason": "timeout"
```

## Why it is abnormal

The fixer did not run out of time: the machine stop ended it, and lym had already recorded its run as interrupted.
`Await` in `internal/gatefixer/await.go` checks the elapsed time since spawn before it checks whether the strand is live,
so any fixer interrupted by a stop that outlasts its timeout is reported as `timeout` instead of `died`.
The writer and anyone reading the record are sent looking for a slow fixer or a timeout that is too short.

The dead record also stays in the visit's set, which `internal/gatefixer/rowgate.go` counts against the fixer budget.
The interrupted fixer's session is not resumed, so the failure it was given falls back to the writer.

## What to do

- Report a fixer whose run is marked interrupted, or whose strand is gone across a reboot, as interrupted or `died`, not `timeout`.
- Consider resuming its session, or spawning a replacement that does not use up the budget, as is done for interrupted run agents.

Provenance: task `sandbox-without-new-kernel`, note `loom-halt.md`.


# A died bouncer judge session spends Code-Bouncer's bounce budget

Imported from [issue #239](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/239).

On a flaky network, Code-Bouncer's judge session twice failed to start: shuttle logged 'provider never became ready; strand torn down', relaunched, and the second run finished at once with no transcript. shedadapters then logged 'bouncer judge run did not complete ... outcome=died', and the row stopped with 'bounce budget exhausted for Code-Bouncer'. The judge never gave a verdict, so no bounce happened, yet the run stalled until a manual `lym loom resume`.

Expected: a judge that dies before giving a verdict is relaunched, or the row halts as an infrastructure failure, without spending the bounce budget meant for real verdicts.

# tender revive reads Claude Code placeholder after an API error as a typed draft and skips the session

## Seen

On 2026-11-26 two Claude sessions stalled on `API Error: Connection refused (ECONNREFUSED)`: `ly:rc-click-wrong-client-session:darn` and `ly:async-run-pusher:code-burler-fix`.
`lym tender revive` skipped both with reason `the input box holds a draft: "Resend your message to try again"`.
That text is Claude Code's own prompt after an API error, not text anyone typed, so revive never reaches the case it exists for.
No code on `origin/main` names the string.

## Workaround

The orch paused each run with `lym batten pause <slug>` and resumed it with `lym batten run <slug>`, which relaunches the row's agent on its own session.

## Expected

The input-box reader in `internal/shuttleengine/claudeengine` treats Claude Code's post-error prompt as an empty box, and `tender revive` gives the session its carry-on line.


# Shuttle idle check reports no input box on an idle seat, killing Plan-Burler-Review

Imported from [issue #219](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/219).

## What happened

The `Plan-Burler-Review` row (`burler-review`) halted `failed` (anomaly `producer-hard-failure`) after round 3: two consecutive `died` outcomes, both "review never started".
Each attempt's seat start ended with:

```
shuttle: deliver the prompt after loading skills: shuttle: the session is not idle: strand "<id>": no input box is on screen; a menu or picker may be open; retry once the session is idle.
```

The pane lines quoted in the same error show the opposite: the skill-load reply `ok scribe:prose, scribe:code-quality, scribe:testing` had finished, a `done` status line was printed, and the `❯` input prompt plus the `bypass permissions on` footer were on screen.
The session was idle with an input box; the idle check reported none.
It happened on attempts 3 and 3b, in two separate halts, with the same pane text each time (`Sautéed for 3s`, `Cogitated for 3s`, `Cooked for 2s` status lines).

## Why abnormal

The seat was healthy.
A false "no input box" reading kills a seat that never got its prompt, burns the review rounds, and halts the whole run as `failed`.
The error text itself says "retry once the session is idle", yet the shuttle did not retry after the capture showed an idle pane.

## What to do

Check the input-box detection in the shuttle's deliver-after-skills step against a pane whose last lines are a completed skill-load reply, a `✻ <verb> for Ns · done` line, the `❯` prompt and the permissions footer.
Retry the idle check for a short window before declaring `died`, so a repaint race right after the skill-load reply does not kill the seat.

Provenance: task `models-torque-drag-adapter`; notes `loom-halt-2.md`, `loom-halt-3.md`.


# Review findings carried over from two landings

## Strand pane memory cap (`10ae7e112`)

- The degraded-launch Warn, on a host without the memory controller delegated to the user manager, has no test of its own.
- The OOM notice can name an earlier kill, or the wrong process, when several panes share a cgroup or the journal line lands after the kill is counted; a shared cgroup is only partly covered.
- The notice's delivery to the parent orch is untested end to end.
- The OOM step reads the strands, which waits on the operation lock; check that it does not stall the watchdog loop.

## Resume after a crash (`dfade5f9a`)

- `removeSupersededStrands` (`internal/shuttleengine/attach.go`) records a superseded running strand's stop as interrupted; check a test covers that path.
- The start retry loop (`internal/shuttleengine/run.go`) reuses the resume on a retried start; a resumed start that fails to come up should retry fresh.

entries.title: Background pushes retry quietly; landing pushes and reads retry instead of failing
entries.body:
## Decisions (operator, 2026-11-26)

- No mail per failed push. lym retries quietly with backoff.
  One summary notice goes to the orch when owed work has stayed unpushed past a threshold (30 minutes proposed), listing every branch still owed, and one notice when all is pushed again.
- The reed status bar shows one field, `sync: <minutes>`: the minutes since this machine last had nothing owed to origin, so the operator sees before switching machines whether work is still only local.
- Agents may still push, but a push of theirs that fails never stops them: their instructions say a failed push needs no action, since lym pushes their commits later, and no row or gate requires an agent's commits to be on origin.
- lym pushes everything it owns through the one pusher with these rules: both branches of every pair, beam branches and the board. Branches the operator made outside lym are left alone.
- How often lym pushes is config in seconds, adaptive: a short interval while pushes go through (60 s proposed), doubled after each failed push up to a ceiling (300 s to start with), and back to the short one after a push lands.
  The reed field shows the interval in force beside the minutes since the last sync, such as `sync: 3m · 60s`.
- A landing makes lym push at once, but a network outage never stops other work: other runs go on committing locally.
  A landing that needs no GitHub call merges locally and hands its owed push to the pusher; one that needs GitHub, such as a pull request, waits for the network and retries, and never fails on a transient error.
- A refusal that retrying cannot fix (rejected push, expired login, moved branch) stops at once with one notice.

## Operator intent (2026-11-26)

LoomYard stops too often because a push to origin fails, above all on VPN at work.
lym and the agents only commit; lym pushes in the background when it suits and retries a failed push later, with fewer pushes and less traffic.
A finished task is the exception: its landing is pushed at once, so a milestone never stays only local.

## What `async-run-pusher` (`b4236816a`) already built

Run transitions commit locally, and a per-worktree pusher started by each commit, the dobby's tick and a resume pushes both sides, retries owed pushes with backoff and posts one notice after a minute.
Read first what each part below still needs on top of it:
`lym fabric commit`'s and `lym board sync`'s own detached pushes, the synchronous landing pushes and GitHub reads, and Seed-IDE's check of the code tip on origin.
A part the pusher already settles is named as such in the change description and dropped.

Bundled from the notes below; each part keeps its note's text.

# Periodic async push of pairs whatever made the commits

Imported from [issue #247](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/247).

## Idea

Agents should only have to commit; they should never have to think about pushing.
lym takes care of every push itself, asynchronously, without blocking an agent.

## Seen

lym already pushes asynchronously after `lym fabric commit`, but only then.
An agent that commits with plain `git commit` leaves its commits unpushed until some later lym step pushes the pair, and the push failures that follow land on whichever step happens to push next.

## Proposal

A periodic pusher in lym, for example in the dobby or its own small daemon, that pushes each live pair's code and records branches when they are ahead of origin, however the commits were made.

- Periodic and not aggressive: a fixed interval of minutes, not a push per commit.
- Never blocks an agent or a row; a failed push is retried at the next period, with backoff, and reported once rather than per attempt.
- Rows that need origin current, such as Finalize, still push synchronously as now.


# Transient push failures are mailed to the orch one by one instead of retried

Imported from [issue #238](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/238).

On a network that resets HTTPS connections now and then (git exits 128 with 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer'), every failed background push sends the orch a creel message naming `lym fabric push` or `lym board sync` as the way forward. In one hour on one hub the orch got eight such messages, for the bolt branch main, task code branches and records branches, and each retry by hand succeeded at once or failed again only because the connection was still flaky.

Expected: fabric retries a transport failure itself with backoff, and mails the orch only once retries are exhausted. One message then covers every branch still unpushed, rather than one message per push. The next pair push already carries a withheld code side, so a single summary would suffice.

Related: #193 (closed), which made runs retry transient fetch failures; pushes have no such retry.

# Unreachable origin halts the run as failed repeatedly instead of one retryable stop

Imported from [issue #243](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/243).

An unreachable origin halted the run as `failed` with anomaly `producer-hard-failure` seven times in a row, across PR-Review and Finalize, instead of waiting or blocking once.

What happened:
- PR-Review and Finalize halted with `landingshed: ... push the task branch ... fabricengine: ls-remote of <task>-weft ... Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`.
- Finalize then halted three more times with `landingshed: Finalize: read who owns the run: board: origin is unreachable, so the owner write was not pushed: fetching origin for the board ... failed (gitrepo: ... git exited 128 ...)`.
- One halt in between was `blocked` with anomaly `escalation-to-human`: `owner check: origin was unreachable, so who owns this run could not be judged; re-run "lym loom resume" in the task worktree once origin answers`.
- Each halt wrote a note and a history entry; the history shows `Finalize / stuck` then `Finalize / goto` before each re-failure.

Why it is abnormal:
- A transient network failure is classed as a hard failure, the same class as a producer defect, and the run state becomes `failed`.
- The same condition surfaced under three different halt shapes (`failed`, `blocked`, `failed`), so the operator cannot tell one outage from three problems.
- Each re-step re-ran immediately and failed again within about a minute, so the retries consumed attempts without waiting for the remote.

What to do:
- Classify unreachable-origin errors (ls-remote, fetch exit 128, connection reset) as one retryable or `blocked` kind with a single note, and have the driver wait or back off before re-stepping.
- Keep `failed` for errors that retrying cannot fix.

Provenance: task `retire-d9`; notes loom-halt-3.md, loom-halt-4.md, loom-halt-5.md, loom-halt-6.md, loom-halt-7.md, loom-halt-8.md, loom-halt-9.md.


# Finalize halts as hard failure on a GitHub API EOF that lym marks transient

Imported from [issue #240](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/240).

A `lym loom step` at the Finalize producer read a pull request's status from the GitHub API and got `unexpected EOF`.
The step was refused with `transient=github-api`, yet the run halted as `failed` with anomaly `producer-hard-failure`.

Quoted from the trace:

```
level=WARN msg="shed: step refused" kind=producer transient=github-api error="landingshed: Finalize: read the pull request's status: pullrequest: read pull request #54: Get \"https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/54\": unexpected EOF"
```

Halt note text: `loom halted failed at Finalize`, `state: failed`, `anomaly: producer-hard-failure`, 15 history entries, all earlier steps done or skipped.

This is abnormal because lym itself labels the error transient, and a single dropped connection to the API then ends a run that had finished every earlier step.
Other network failures in the same run (an unreachable origin before a push) were retried until they landed, so the Finalize read is inconsistent with them.

Suggested fix: when a step is refused with a non-empty `transient` kind, retry it with backoff, or leave the run resumable, instead of recording `producer-hard-failure`.
A failure of this kind should reach `failed` only after the retry budget is spent.

Provenance: task `transient-tripout-overpull`, from `loom-halt-2.md`.


# Seed-IDE fails the run when the task branch's detached push has not landed yet

Imported from [issue #218](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/218).

Import note: the issue names files under `.lym/`, which is deleted with its worktree, so only what the issue quotes of them reached the board: `.lym/logs`.

## What happened

Run `weekly-time-report` (recipe raddle, promoted from a Sketch) stopped at Seed-IDE with:

> run "weekly-time-report" cannot act: the code tip e7b0cc2 the run's last transition names is not on origin yet; way forward: run "lym batten run weekly-time-report" again once the code push lands

Timeline from `.lym/logs` (2026-11-24, CET):

- 14:45:52 Worktree-Create done; the task branch forks from the prime's local `main` at e7b0cc2, one commit ahead of `origin/main`.
- 14:45:52 and 14:45:55 fabricengine spawned detached pushes of the new pair (`fabric --warp-path …/weekly-time-report …`).
- 14:45:57 Seed-IDE's bootstrap checked whether e7b0cc2 is on origin, found it was not, and refused the step.
- Shortly after, the detached push landed: `git ls-remote origin` showed `refs/heads/weekly-time-report` at e7b0cc2.

The network was slow and resetting that day (`Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` on records pushes), so the detached push took longer than the 2–5 s gap.

## Effect

- The run stopped as failed, and the tackler handed it back to the parent asking whether to push the prime's `main`, which was not needed.
- A plain `lym batten run weekly-time-report` afterwards went straight through Seed-IDE to Run-Shed.

## Expected

A check that the code tip is on origin, right after lym itself spawned the push that puts it there, should wait for that push, or retry for a while, instead of failing the run.
The stop should also say that lym's own push of the task branch is in flight, so the tackler does not ask the parent to push the parent branch.


# Finalize blocks on untracked leftovers of a project the merge-in deleted

Imported from [issue #242](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/242).

## Seen

A darn run's Finalize merged its parent beam into the task worktree after its pull request had merged on GitHub.
The beam had just taken in a main commit that deleted a whole C# project.
The task worktree still held that project's directory with only untracked, gitignored content: `bin/`, `obj/` and generated fixtures.
Once git removed the tracked files, the directory was no longer ignored by the deleted `.gitignore`, so it showed as untracked.
Finalize then blocked: "the task worktree has uncommitted changes after the merge-in: …/NORCE.Import.CommonLibHarness/; commit or remove them on the task branch, then resume".

The run had no live agent left to remove it.
The orch may not edit a task worktree, and the Go driver only asked the parent a question and stopped again on resume.
The only ways forward were a goto back to the writer, which would re-run review and PR rows for a merged pull request, or the operator removing the directory by hand.

## Workaround

The operator removes the leftover directory by hand, then the orch runs `lym loom resume` in the task worktree.

## Expected

Finalize's merge-in treats a directory that holds only files the merge's base ignored, under a path the merge deleted, as leftover output:
it removes it, or ignores it in the clean-tree check, and goes on.
Failing that, the stop names a lym verb the parent can run to clear it, instead of needing a hand edit in the task worktree.



# Seen 2026-11-26: a busy push lock fails a dobby start

With several tasks released at once, dobby's catch-up for `sandbox-closed-area-build` and `keep-landed-records` failed with `fabricengine: push lock busy: .../loomyard-weft/.weft/fabric.push.lock still held after 30s ... neither side was pushed`, and each needed a manual `lym batten run`.
A held push lock is contention, not a failure: the catch-up should hand the owed push to the pusher and start the run.

# Review findings carried over from `async-run-pusher` (`b4236816a`)

Code-Review left these MEDIUM findings open; check each and close what is still open:

- tests of the pusher's lock and start conditions (`internal/runpusher`);
- tests of the pusher restart calls from the dobby tick and the batten and loom resumes (`internal/beamcli`, `internal/battencli`, `internal/loomcli`);
- tests of the teardown's push and level wiring (`teardownPushSeams` in `internal/battencli/wire.go`);
- Worktree-Teardown looping with pushes off (`internal/battenshed/teardown.go`).


## From issue #254

Imported from [issue #254](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/254).

## What happened

A `lym shed` run halted `failed` with anomaly `interrupted-stop` at producer `Webster`.
The note says a machine stop likely ended the loop, which is not itself a defect.
The stderr it carries shows two things that are:

1. The step wrote `status push is owed; retrying until it lands` for `producer=Drift-Expect` while origin was unreachable (`ls-remote` failed with `Connection reset by peer`).
   It then logged `origin is unreachable before a push; pushing unchecked, so the push's own failure is recorded` twice, about 10 s apart.
   The loop never produced an envelope, and the halt note was written only about 20 hours after the loop started, after the machine rebooted.
   Nothing in the notes shows a bound on the retry, or any record of the push's own failure after the "pushing unchecked" lines.
2. The note says step `Drift-Await` was in flight, while the stderr's producer is `Drift-Expect` and the history shows both `Drift-Await` and `Drift-Expect` as `skipped`.
   The in-flight step name and the producer that owed the push disagree.

Quoted lines (paths removed):

```
level=WARN msg="loomcli: status push is owed; retrying until it lands" producer=Drift-Expect state=running error="fabricengine: push code side ...: ls-remote of <branch> ...: exit 128: fatal: unable to access '<origin>': Recv failure: Connection reset by peer; way forward: run `lym fabric push` ... to retry the push"
level=WARN msg="loomcli: origin is unreachable before a push; pushing unchecked, so the push's own failure is recorded"
level=WARN msg="loomcli: origin is unreachable before a push; pushing unchecked, so the push's own failure is recorded"
```

## Why it is abnormal

A transient network failure on a status push should either land after a bounded retry or fail the step with a recorded push error.
An unbounded wait with no outcome stalls the whole run until something external kills it, and the halt then reads as a machine stop instead of a push problem.

## What to do

- Bound the "push is owed" retry, and record the push's final failure in the step's status and trace when it gives up.
- Make the halt note's in-flight step and the producer owing the push name the same step, or say why they differ.

Provenance: task `models-bit-rock-formation`, from `loom-halt-2.md`.

entries.title: A beam member's run names its beam orch as parent, which may amend the beam's record
entries.body:
Bundled from the notes below; each part keeps its note's text.

# A beam member's run records the prime orch as its parent orch

Imported from [issue #232](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/232).

## Seen

In the DrillOpPlan hub on 2026-11-24, the run `models-stick-slip-map`, a member of the beam `models-torque-drag` and spawned from the beam's worktree, records the prime's orch `dop:orch` as its parent orch.
Its PR-Review sent the `[pr-review request]` for PR #52 (into the beam branch `hanf/models-torque-drag`) to `dop:orch`, as ask 1 from the PR-Review session and as ask 2 from `dop:LOOM`.
The beam's orch `dop:models-torque-drag:orch`, which owns and released the run, reviewed the PR, and its answer was refused:

```
caller dop:models-torque-drag:orch is neither the run's parent orch nor the strand the ask went to
```

The beam's dobby sends its notices for the same run to `dop:orch` too.
Knatte18/loomyard#231 shows the same gap in the tackler and driver prompts of a beam member.

## Expected

A beam member's run records the beam's orch as its parent orch, so its parent-review asks, notices and escalations go to the beam's orch and that orch's answer is accepted.

## Workaround

The prime orch forwards each ask and notice to the beam's orch, and runs `lym loom parent-review answer <slug> --ask <n> --satisfied` in the task worktree on the beam orch's verdict.


# Tackler and driver prompts of a beam member say no parent is recorded

Imported from [issue #231](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/231).

## Seen

In the DrillOpPlan hub on 2026-11-10, the shed tackler of run `models-backend`, a member of the beam `adopt-models-sim`, got a prompt whose section "Your parent" read:

```
No parent is recorded for this run.
When you are blocked, write your report and stop.
```

The run had a parent: the beam's orch `dop:adopt-models-sim:orch`, which owned and released it.
Other tackler and driver prompts in the hub carried the same text, in the form "No parent is recorded for the run, so the question is written for whoever owns it."
The tackler escalated on a merge conflict and stopped; the prime orch saw the stop and passed it to the beam orch by hand.

## Expected

The tackler and driver prompts of a beam member name the beam's orch as the parent, so a blocked tackler or driver reaches it directly.

## Workaround

The prime orch forwards a beam member's stop to the beam's orch by creel.


# Beam orch cannot amend its own beam's decision record

Imported from [issue #236](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/236).

## What happened

In hub `dop`, beam `models-torque-drag` (P1) holds a stored decision record.
On 2026-11-24 the operator made a decision that supersedes two of its decisions: a new member task maps the well's formation strength into the Models bit-rock law, where the beam record's D1 and D2 keep Models' bit-rock defaults.
The member's Discussion saw the conflict and asked the beam orch, which owns the beam record, to settle it.

The beam orch could not amend its own beam's record:

- `lym loom decision add models-torque-drag --by parent ...` from the beam orch refused: `the caller "dop:models-torque-drag:orch" is a task session; way forward: a design call after the Discussion is the parent's to record; ask dop:orch to run the verb`.
  The beam orch is an orch, not a task session, and it is the record's owner.
- `lym board upsert --record-file` refuses an entry a run holds, and a beam's project is always held by its pawl run (`running · Beam-Await`), so that way is closed for the beam's whole life.

## Expected

The beam's own orch can append a decision to, or replace, its beam's decision record while the beam lives, as a run's parent can for a task's record.
The caller check counts a beam orch (`<hub>:<beam>:orch`) as an orch, not as a task session.

## Related

The same misclassification of the beam orch shows in parent-review: `lym loom parent-review answer` refuses the beam orch for its member's pull request (`neither the run's parent orch nor the strand the ask went to`), filed by the hub orch as Knatte18/loomyard#232.




## From issue #252

Imported from [issue #252](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/252).

A beam orch received a PR-Review pause notice for a task of its beam, naming 'lym tender resume <slug>' as the way forward. Run from the beam orch's session, 'lym tender resume <slug>' was refused: 'pause: an agent may pause, resume or revive only its own pair; way forward: ask your parent session'. The beam orch is the task's parent. Workaround: the prime orch ran the resume. Expected: the parent orch of a task, beam orch included, may resume its tasks' tender pauses, or the notice names a way forward open to it.

## From issue #251

Imported from [issue #251](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/251).

A task's PR-Review agent paused its own pair with lym tender pause before a push. The beam orch, which parents that task, then could not lift the pause: lym tender resume <task-slug> from the beam orch's session is refused with 'an agent may pause, resume or revive only its own pair'. Mail from the beam orch to the paused agent is not delivered while the pause holds, so the run stays stuck until the prime orch runs the resume.

Expected: the orch that parents a run may resume that run's pair, as it is the session that settles the run's halts.

entries.title: Close a task's scope at Code-Review, and catch earlier what a PR review found
entries.body:
This task builds the scope note and items 3 to 6 of the Describe-text note's Idea; items 1 and 2 landed with `describe-review-and-sync`.

Bundled from the notes below; each part keeps its note's text.

# Close the scope of a task when its first Code-Review round starts, and have lym hold the line

Imported from [issue #226](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/226).

## Seen (operator, 2026-11-24)

A task's scope can still change late.
In the C# hubs a parent orch recorded decisions that widened a task while the run was at PR-Review, after Code-Review had finished, and the reviewers never judged the diff against the widened record.
In one run Code-Review stopped at its round cap because a decision finding spawns no fixer, so the widening was in the record but never built.

The operator's rule: decisions go in as early as possible, and once the Code-Review perch has begun it is too late.
The last Code-Review round is the last link that can change anything.
What comes up after that becomes a note for a new task, not a change to this one.

## Idea

Close a task's scope when its first Code-Review round starts, and have lym hold the line, so it is not only a rule for the parent orch.

- Before the line, a decision enters the record as an `Added after Discussion` entry, and `code-scope` and the plan lenses read it.
- After the line, no decision enters the record.
  `lym loom decision add` (and `replace`) refuse once the run stands at or past the first Code-Review round, and the refusal names the way forward: file the call as a note for a new task.
  The refusal reaches the parent and the agent the way the other `decision add` refusals do.
- Two things stay outside the line: feedback from a person through the PR agent, and the mechanical fixes Finalize makes to a merge or test failure.
- The orch procedure and the parent's prompt say the same, so the parent files a note instead of trying.
- Read first how `lym loom decision add` decides where a run stands (`internal/loomcli/decision.go` already refuses at some stages), where the Drift rows sit against the Code-Review perch, whether a Drift verdict can send a run back past the line, and how darn, tapestry and arras recipes place their Code-Review perch.
- Related issues: taking the parent out of PR-Review, and reviewing the Describe text and catching the rest of the parent's findings earlier.


# Review the Describe text inside the Describe row, and catch the rest of what the parent finds at PR-Review earlier

Imported from [issue #225](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/225).

## Seen (operator, 2026-11-24)

In the C# repos on one machine, a parent asked to review a PR always finds something.
That points to a design flaw: if the parent finds something, an earlier quality check missed it.

The operator's guess was that the delivered code often does not cover everything the Discussion's decision record asked for.
The operator judges the finding below, that most of it is the PR text, as not very important, and that it is solved by reviewing the Describe text too.

## What the parent finds (analysis, 2026-11-24)

An analysis read 25 PR-Review rounds with findings, across four hubs; one more hub had no PR-Review records.
About 65 findings are itemised in readable text; about 29 more were in scratchpad files that no longer exist.
The task worktrees and the Sketches of the landed tasks are gone, so the only full source is each hub's creel mail journal, and the gate attributions are mostly inferred.
The full report is a local file and is not committed.

- About half of the findings (32 of 65) are about the PR description, not the code:
  internal process or tool names in the text (12), wrong or overreaching claims (12), and content the task asked for that the text omits (8).
- The rest are tests missing or too costly (10), wrong behaviour (8), doc or comment drift (7) and scope the Sketch did not hold (8).
- The operator's guess holds only in part: 4 of 25 rounds cite a Sketch or task requirement that was missed, and all four concern the PR text or scope, not code behaviour.
- A finding is often sent twice because the agent edits the summary file but not the GitHub PR body (about 5 rounds).

## Idea

The Describe row writes the change description, which becomes the PR title, the PR body and the landing commit message.
It is a seat table (`DescribeTable` in `internal/landingshed/describe.go`) whose session already reads the decision record, and its only gate is mechanical (`ValidateDescription`); no agent reviews what the text says.

1. Review the Describe text inside the Describe row with a second agent, an assistant seat, and send its findings back to the writer; Describe is the last step that uses an LLM, so no review runs after it.
   The reviewer checks that the text names no internal process or tool (board, task, scoper, Sketch, decision record, "item N of"), that every claim holds against the diff and the task's report or measurements, and that every deliverable the Sketch says to state in the description is there.
   The mechanical gate stays in front of it.
   This covers the 32 findings about the text.
2. Sync the GitHub PR body from the description on every push, and verify the two match (about 5 re-sent rounds).
3. Run the mutation or redundancy tier on every C# task, and give the Plan a tier0 cost budget (10 test findings).
4. Have Discussion record what the parent will check: measured figures, doc statements and test intent.
5. Let a Code-Review finding the parent already ruled in scope reach a fixer; today a decision finding spawns none.
6. Re-check a constant quoted in a doc when the case it was measured on changes.

The issue on taking the parent out of PR-Review leaves these checks to the cold-start reviewers, so they must run before PR-Review, and a task's scope closes at its first Code-Review round (see the issue on closing a task's scope).

entries.title: Cross-machine mail into the receiving orch own channel instead of a channel per orch pair
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-11-26, relayed by norce:orch on osl46)

The first cross-machine test over the Slack bridge worked both ways (Neve #2650, osl46 #129).
Setup was clumsy: `approve <machine>` by name failed, and each side needed `approve <machine> <app id>`.
Bridge channels are made per pair of orchs, so their number grows with the square of the orchs and machines.

## Idea

One inbound channel per orch: its existing channel.
An orch on another machine posts its mail into the receiver's channel.
The receiving relay checks the sender bot's app id against the approved peers, as today.
Channels then grow linearly.

Cost and open points:

- A conversation between A and B is split across two channels.
  A could mirror its outgoing mail into its own channel, or the two could use threads, so the operator sees the whole exchange in one place.
- The relay must keep telling the operator's messages apart from peer bots' posts in the same channel.
- Why approve by name found no bot `lym-neve` is unexplained; a design that still names peers must find them.

The operator will think further about it; this is a note, not a task.

entries.title: Name config keys as <module>.<path> in Go comments, and guard string literals for bare keys
entries.body:
After `config-keys-nested` nests the config keys by area, about 525 Go comment lines in about 199 files, plus single-word keys on top, still name a template key bare.
PATTERN-config-key-names asks that such a comment say `<module>.<path>`.

Deferred from T3 code review round 1, finding F1, to keep that run short.


## From issue #265

Imported from [issue #265](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/265).

## What happened

A code review finding asked for a repository-wide sweep of config key names written without their module, and no tool finds them.
A grep over the underscored template keys was the only practical method.
It missed single-word keys such as `engine` and `scoper`, and any key that ended a string literal, so messages were reported done while several were not.
Self-check forks caught the misses.

An earlier implementer had also found bare key names in messages and help texts outside its card's packages:
`gatecli`, `batcher`, `battencli`, `beamcli`, `webstercli`, `hibernatecli`, `reportcli`, `preflightshed`,
`weaverengine` (`ResolveLadder` and `settingRefusal`), `sheddriver/tackler.go`, `shedarbiter`, `burlerengine/fix.go` and `loomshed/plancontext.go`.
Some of these may have been fixed since.

## Why it is abnormal

A message or help text naming a key without its module can regress at any time, and nothing detects it mechanically.

## What to do

Add a guard test that scans Go string literals for a config template's key names written without their module.

Provenance: task `config-keys-nested`, notes `burler-code-r1.md`, `11-module-key-messages.md`.

entries.title: Card gate runs only the card's listed packages, so a wider intent breaks tests unseen
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #263](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/263).

## What happened

A card's stated intent covered every remaining message of one kind across the repository, but its edit list named a fixed set of packages and its card gate ran only those.
Tests outside the list that assert on the changed messages failed unseen by the gate (in `burlercli`, `shuttleengines`, `configcli` and `loomengine`).
The implementer found them only by testing extra packages by hand.

A related miss in the preceding card: a key the card attributed to `loomengine` and `loomcli` is set in `internal/shedrecipe`, which was not among the card's targets.

## Why it is abnormal

The card gate passes while the change breaks tests, so the failure surfaces later or not at all within the card.
Plan writing and plan review accepted an intent broader than the card's targets.

## What to do

- Have the card gate also run the packages whose tests depend on the changed packages, or on the changed strings.
- Have plan review reject a repository-wide intent whose edit list is a fixed set of packages with no step that proves the set complete.

Provenance: task `config-keys-nested`, notes `11-module-key-messages.md`, `10-loom-key-messages.md`.


## From issue #262

Imported from [issue #262](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/262).

## What happened

A plan had two cards that each add an exported function whose first caller is a later card.
The tier1 guard `TestTestOnlyCode_EveryProductionFunctionIsReachableFromAMain` rejected each at its card gate.
The implementer allowlisted each function in its own commit with a `Loosened-Check:` trailer.
One allowlist entry was still present at the end of the batch, and the card that adds its caller has to remember to delete it, since a stale entry fails the guard.

## Why it is abnormal

An ordinary helper-then-caller card split cannot pass the card gate without loosening a check.
The loosening and its later removal are hand work that no step of the plan states.

## What to do

Either have plan writing and plan review keep a new function and its first caller in one card,
or let the card gate tolerate a function whose caller a later card of the same plan declares.

Provenance: task `config-keys-nested`, note `01-config-key-name.md`.

entries.title: Flaky gate: TestGateTestMap/NamedPackageIsRebuiltWhenFresh reports an unexpected PassedAlone entry under load
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #260](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/260).

## What happened

A verify gate failed on `TestGateTestMap/NamedPackageIsRebuiltWhenFresh` (`internal/gatecli`, tier 1), on a branch that touched nothing in `internal/gatecli` or `internal/testcover`.

The only mismatch was one extra entry: the fixture test `alpha.TestAlphaTwo` was reported as passing only when run by itself.

```
tier1 (exit 1):
  github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/internal/gatecli TestGateTestMap/NamedPackageIsRebuiltWhenFresh:
    internal/gatecli/testmap_integration_test.go:1124: runTestMap() mismatch (-want +got):
    gatecli.testMapOutcome{
    ... // 1 ignored and 2 identical fields
    TimedOut:    {"alpha.TestAlphaHangs"},
    FailedTests: {"alpha.TestAlphaHangs"},
    - 	PassedAlone: nil,
    + 	PassedAlone: []string{"alpha.TestAlphaTwo"},
    LeftOut:     {},
    Exit:        1,
    ... // 1 ignored field
    }
```

The same subtest passed in the run's other verify logs, and the `TestGateTestMap` run alone through `lym gate test --tier 1` passed.

## Why it is abnormal

A gate goes red on a test the change does not reach, and the agent has to spend a round deciding whether the failure is its own.

## What to do

The likely cause, not confirmed, is load: the test runs with a shortened per-test limit, and a healthy fixture test can exceed it in a full run.
Make the healthy fixture tests insensitive to that limit under load, for example by separating the limit that `TestAlphaHangs` must exceed from the one the other fixture tests run under, or by widening the margin.

Provenance: task `audit-flags-master-friction`, note `burler-code-r1.md`.

entries.title: batten cancel --remove of a beam leaves the project's beam flag set
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #259](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/259).

A beam was made with lym beam create <slug> from the prime, then ended before any member ran with lym batten cancel <slug> --remove. The cancel ended the pawl run and removed the pair and its records, but the board project kept "beam": true and had status draft.

The flag cannot be cleared afterwards. lym board upsert '{"slug":"<slug>","beam":false}' is refused: 'the beam flag stays set for the beam's life, which ends when lym beam land <slug> lands it'. But the beam has no pair and no run left to land. The only way back to a plain project was to detach the members, remove the project, upsert it again and re-attach the members and their depends_on, which changes the project's handle.

The cancel also warned: 'the beam's orch was not stopped: lym orch runs from the hub's prime worktree or a beam; "<slug>" is neither', which shows the cancel no longer saw the entry as a beam once the pair was gone.

Expected: batten cancel --remove of a beam's pawl run ends the beam's life and clears the project's beam flag, leaving a plain project whose members are untouched. Alternatively, a verb such as lym beam cancel <slug> does so.

entries.title: Whole-repo guards run at landing, and the dead-code check with the board tidy, not in every task gate
entries.body:
## Seen (2026-11-26)

`cmd/lym`'s test binary reaches about 2 GB and is the binary the gate's memory guard kills first when the machine is short.
Its tests build few hubs (7 `CopyHub` calls); most are guard tests that read the whole repository's source.
The heaviest is the tier1 test `TestTestOnlyCode_EveryProductionFunctionIsReachableFromAMain` in `cmd/lym/testonlycode_linux_test.go`:
it loads every package with `packages.LoadAllSyntax` and builds an SSA call graph of the whole program to find code only tests reach.
`cmd/lym` imports nearly every package, so nearly every change puts it in the gate's impacted set, and the whole-repo guards run in every task gate.

## Idea (operator, 2026-11-26)

- Whole-repo guards that catch a break, such as tree-sitter linking and the cross-compile check, leave the task gates and run once at landing.
- The dead-code check, the call-graph test above, leaves the gates altogether and runs with the periodic upkeep:
  dobby already spawns the board-tidy agent every `board_tidy_every` landings (`internal/dobbyengine`).
  At that point the check runs on the main branch, and each dead function it finds becomes a note on the board.
  Dead code breaks nothing, so finding it a few landings late costs little.
- Find every whole-repo guard in `cmd/lym` and name for each where it runs: at landing or with the tidy.

entries.title: Evaluate the coverage maps (testmap), every user of them and what each gives, and whether to remove them
entries.body:
## Why (operator, 2026-11-26)

Much effort went into the per-test coverage maps, and little use has been found for them.
The measurement in `docs/research/speed/testmap-use-measure-2026-11-21/report.md` found, over 10 darn runs:
the reach turn added tests in 2 runs; the mutation step raised 6 LOW findings from 27 survivors; the "reaches none" triage line was wrong every time and is removed;
reach and mutation together cost about 2 minutes of gate wall time per run.

## Done meanwhile (operator, 2026-11-26)

The mutation report step is off in every gate key of the loomyard hub's `gate.yaml` (`reports` without `mutation`; `webster-fix` and `pr-review` with `reports: []`).
Reach and redundancy stay on.

## What to find out

- Every user of the coverage maps in lym: the reach, redundancy and mutation report steps, `lym gate mutate`, `lym gate test --map`, and any other reader.
- For each: what it has given in landed runs (tests added, findings raised and fixed) against what it costs in gate time, memory and upkeep.
- The effect of turning the mutation step off: whether review findings, or the defects that land, change in the runs after it.
- A recommendation per user: keep, tune or remove; and whether the maps themselves, `internal/testcover` and their upkeep, go when no user is kept.

- Through what lym reads and sets a window's virtual desktop and tile on KDE Plasma (KWin scripting, D-Bus), and what it does on other desktops.
- What "kind" a placement rule keys on: hub, role (orch, run strand, board session), or run.
